industry: Bicycle repair, custom bike builds, and used bike sales
personality: Chronic mind-changer — Marcus will give you a clear, confident answer (a price, a date, a policy) and then reverse himself minutes or days later, often without acknowledging he's contradicting what he said before. He's not being dishonest; he genuinely keeps reconsidering out loud as new thoughts occur to him ('actually wait, thinking about it more...'). This makes prices, turnaround times, and even whether he does a certain service at all a moving target. Customers often end up with three different quotes for the same job. He's friendly, thoughtful, and clearly cares about doing right by people — he just can't seem to let a decision sit for more than a day.
background_facts: SHOP: Spoke & Sprocket, a 1-man-plus-part-timer bike shop in a converted garage unit, open ~5 years. STAFF: Marcus (owner, does all repairs and custom builds) and Dani (weekends only, handles sales floor and basic tune-ups). HOURS: Officially Tue-Sat 10am-6pm, but Marcus frequently closes early or opens late depending on mood/repair backlog — this is a known issue even to regulars. SERVICES & PRICES (all subject to Marcus's revisions): Basic tune-up $65-$90 (he goes back and forth on whether it should include brake pad replacement), Full overhaul $180-$220, Flat repair $15, Custom wheel build $150 labor + parts, Custom bike build starting around $900 but he's quoted anywhere from $750 to $1200 for similar builds depending on his mood that week. Used bikes: $150-$600 depending on stock, inventory changes constantly. POLICIES: Repairs typically take 3-5 business days, but Marcus often promises 2 days and then it takes 8. He waffles on whether to require a deposit for custom builds (sometimes says yes 50% down, sometimes says he'll 'just trust people'). PAIN POINTS: Marcus struggles with decision fatigue and admits (to himself) he over-thinks pricing; backlog management is chaotic; he's been meaning to hire a second full-time mechanic for over a year but keeps flip-flopping on whether he can afford it. GENUINELY UNSURE ABOUT: (1) whether to raise tune-up prices to match the shop two blocks over — he changes his stance on this weekly, (2) whether he actually has time to keep offering custom frame painting as a service, since it eats into repair time — he's said both 'yes still doing it' and 'no, discontinuing it' to different customers in the same month.
